You, as part of a __team__, will be responsible for the completion of an open ended final project for this course, the goal of which is to tackle an “interesting” real life problem using the tools and techniques covered in this class. 


# REQUIRED: Project details 

In this week's workshop you will begin on your group projects. This will be the first exploration stage for the project start. It is crucial to finalize the your groups during this week's workshop. You will find all the information you will need about the group projects is available in 

[Project instruction](https://uoe-ids.netlify.app/assessments/project/)

## GitHub repository

One member of your team should be responsible for managing the repository of your group project. This team member should clone the <a id="project_template_repo">project template repository</a> from the course GitHub account and add each of the team members as collaborators. Instructions on how to clone a repository, add collaborators and to create a new version control R project can be found in the lab worksheets.

The project template repository can be found [HERE](https://github.com/uoeIDS/project_template)

## OPTIONAL: Some initial data viz exercises

### Data viz for starwars

Let us start with some basics of data viz on the starwars data set.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
starwars_df <- starwars
```

To decide, how to create any data viz, this supplementary material can be very useful to explore different types with explanations, and R code examples 

[From Data to Viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/)


## Exercise 2.

Modify the following plot to change the color of all points to `"pink"`.

Initial code given as; 

```{r}
ggplot(starwars_df, 
       aes(x = height, y = mass, color = gender, size = birth_year)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue")
```

## Exercise 3

Add labels for title, x and y axes, and size of points. Uncomment to see the effect.

```{r}
ggplot(starwars, 
       aes(x = height, y = mass, color = gender, size = birth_year)) +
  geom_point(color = "#30509C") +
  labs(
    #title = "___",
    #x = "___", 
    #y = "___",
    #___
    )
```
